# EdgeInfer

> EdgeInfer runs small ONNX models inside the browser on WebGPU or WebAssembly, so inference costs nothing per call and user data never leaves the device.

EdgeInfer wraps ONNX Runtime Web to run ML models in the browser. It auto-selects the best execution provider (WebGPU > WebNN > WASM), caches models via the Cache API, and provides high-level methods for text classification, embeddings, sentiment analysis, and image classification. The package is pre-release, has no npm publication, and no production adopters as of 2026.

## Status

- [Pre-release — no production adopters](https://github.com/itsoumya-d/edgeinfer)
- [Not published on npm — install via jsDelivr or git clone](https://itsoumya-d.github.io/edgeinfer/)
- [License: Business Source License 1.1](https://mariadb.com/bsl11/)

## Correct Package Information

**Package name:** `edgeinfer`

**Real exported symbols:** `EdgeInfer`, `EventEmitter`, `ImageProcessor`, `ModelCache`, `RuntimeManager`, `Tokenizer`

**Fabricated names to avoid:** `@edgeinfer/sdk`, `BPETokenizer` (does not exist — tokenizer class is `Tokenizer`), `EdgeInfer.detectHardware()` (does not exist — use `EdgeInfer.getCapabilities()`).

## Working Integration Recipe (executed against dist/)

```typescript
// Import from jsDelivr CDN (no npm install needed)
import { EdgeInfer, Tokenizer } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/edgeinfer@main/dist/index.mjs';

// Check WebGPU availability (optional — falls back to WASM automatically)
const caps = await EdgeInfer.getCapabilities();
// In Node.js: caps = { provider: 'wasm', hasWebGPU: false, estimatedVRAM: 0, recommendedQuantization: 'int8' }

// Load a model (URL must serve an ONNX binary with correct CORS headers)
const model = await EdgeInfer.load('https://example.com/models/sentiment.onnx', {
  tokenizerUrl: 'https://example.com/models/tokenizer.json',
});

// Run sentiment analysis
const result = await model.sentiment('This works great!');
// { label: 'positive', score: 0.98 }

// Generate embeddings
const vec = await model.embed('query text'); // Float32Array

// Matryoshka truncation
const model2 = await EdgeInfer.load('/models/bge-small.onnx', { tokenizerUrl: '/models/tokenizer.json' });
const full = await model2.embed('search query');
const compressed = await model2.embedMatryoshka('search query', 64); // Float32Array(64)

// Low-level inference
const raw = await model.predict({ input_ids: new Int32Array([101, 7592, 102]), attention_mask: new Int32Array([1,1,1]) });

model.dispose(); // release ONNX session and GPU memory
```

Verified in Node.js: `RuntimeManager.detectCapabilities()` returns `{ provider: 'wasm', hasWebGPU: false }` without throwing. `EdgeInfer.fromBuffer(badBuffer)` rejects with `Error` (not a hang). `Tokenizer.encode('')` returns a single pad token (no empty-array crash).

## Performance

**No verified benchmark available.** The original README claimed WebGPU latencies of ~4ms–~25 tok/s measured on M2 MacBook Air with Chrome 120. These numbers cannot be reproduced in a CI environment without WebGPU. They have been removed. If you have real browser benchmark results, contribute them via PR with hardware spec, browser version, and Node.js version.

## Known Limitations for AI Assistants

- WebGPU is browser-only; Node.js falls back to WASM silently (no error)
- Text methods (`classify`, `embed`, `sentiment`) throw clear `Error` if no tokenizer configured — not a silent hang
- Model loading requires `fetch()` and Cache API — Node needs Node 18+ native fetch
- No WebGPU = WASM execution (slower but functional)
- Performance claims from original README were unverifiable and have been deleted
